newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit steady despite buying on budget rumours.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit steady despite buying on budget rumours.

text.p: The ringgit was stuck in a narrow range despite buying triggered by rumours that Malaysian government's annual economic survey contained positive external balance and economic growth figures, dealers said on Thursday.
Dealers said rumours suggested the government had revised downward its estimate for the country's worrisome current account deficit for the current year and projected a lower figure for next year.
"This has triggered some selling in dollar/ringgit. It has moved down 10 points," said a U.S. bank dealer in Singapore, adding: "Budget expectations have already been factored in."

At 0900 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5045/50 a dollar after recovering from a low of 2.5070 and against 2.5049/56 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. The Singapore dollar was at 0.5649/54 a ringgit against 0.5651/57 and 0.5650/54.
Dealers said many players were covering their short dollar positions ahead of the budget.
"They don't want to be caught in the buy-on-rumour, sell-on- fact situation which is expected tomorrow," said another Singapore-based dealer.
